pages.title: Why your sleep gets worse in your forties
body: Sleep architecture changes with age: deep sleep shortens and night waking becomes more frequent.
Researchers point to shifting melatonin rhythms, caffeine sensitivity and late screen use as the main levers people can control.
A consistent wake time does more for sleep quality than a consistent bedtime.
Keeping the bedroom cool, around 18 degrees Celsius, helps most adults fall asleep faster.

pages.title: What a used EV battery report actually tells you
body: A battery health report estimates remaining capacity as a percentage of the original pack.
Fast-charging history and climate matter more than mileage for long-term degradation.
Most packs lose capacity quickly in the first two years and then settle into a slow decline.
Buyers should ask for a recent state-of-health reading rather than relying on the dashboard range estimate.

pages.title: The fastest weeknight pasta that still tastes slow-cooked
body: Blooming tomato paste in olive oil for two minutes builds the deep flavor of a long-simmered sauce.
Starchy pasta water is the binder that turns a thin sauce glossy and clingy.
Finishing the pasta in the pan for the last minute lets it absorb the sauce instead of sitting under it.
A splash of acid at the end, lemon or vinegar, brightens the whole dish.
